title: Adequacy of Healthcare Settings to Handle Next COVID-19 Wave and Steps to Reduce Infection Rate Given Increase in Omicron Variants
what_it_is: Adequacy of Healthcare Settings to Handle Next COVID-19 Wave and Steps to Reduce Infection Rate Given Increase in Omicron Variants

sections.label: COVID-19 steps and healthcare readiness
sections.summary: Questions ask what steps the Ministry will take to reduce infections and encourage senior booster shots, and whether healthcare settings are equipped for the next wave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health in light of the recent rise of COVID-19 infections in Singapore, especially with the increase in the Omicron subvariants infection in the community, what steps will the Ministry take to (i) reduce the infection rate and (ii) encourage seniors to take their second COVID-19 booster shot.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether our healthcare settings are adequately equipped to handle the next COVID-19 wave expected in July or August 2022; and (b) whether the Ministry can provide an update on the redesign of COVID-19 community treatment facilities.

sections.label: Tuesday COVID-19 case numbers
sections.summary: The speaker says Tuesday cases spike, expecting over 12,000, about 10% more than last week, indicating we are near or at the peak.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Tuesday is always the day when cases spike.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We should expect at the end of today case numbers of over 12,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: This is a tad higher than the same time last week, which was over 11,000, 10% more than last week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, there are indications that we are near the peak, if not at the peak.

sections.label: Seniors needing three shots
sections.summary: With more mutations, three shots are needed; about 60,000 seniors aged 60 and above have not taken their first booster, down from 70,000 last week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: With more mutations, we now need three shots.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: There are about 60,000 seniors aged 60 and above who have not taken their first booster or third shot.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: This number has come down from last week, when Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and I announced that there were 70,000.

sections.label: COVID-19 Treatment Facility beds
sections.summary: Sufficient beds are maintained in COVID-19 Treatment Facilities for serious cases not needing hospital care, recently consolidated from about 2,000-over beds to about 1,300 with higher manning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We have also maintained sufficient beds in our COVID-19 Treatment Facilities, or CTFs, to manage serious cases that do not need hospital care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We have recently consolidated our CTFs from about 2,000-over beds, to about 1,300 beds, but with a higher manning ratio.

sections.label: Oral antivirals at polyclinics
sections.summary: As of 30 June, all polyclinics and 103 participating PHPCs can prescribe oral antivirals to clinically-eligible patients in the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As of 30 June, all polyclinics and 103 participating PHPCs can prescribe oral antivirals to clinically-eligible patients in the community.

sections.label: COVID-19 treatment subsidies and PHPCs
sections.summary: As at end FY2021, the Government spent about $730 million on subsidising inpatient and $220 million on outpatient COVID-19 treatments, and has stood up over 1,000 PHPCs since February 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As at end FY2021, the Government has spent about $730 million and $220 million on subsidising inpatient and outpatient treatments for COVID-19 respectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Since February 2020, we have progressively stood up more than 1,000 PHPCs.

sections.label: BA.4 and BA.5 subvariants
sections.summary: About 50% of current infections are the BA.4 or BA.5 subvariants, mostly BA.5.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Of all infections now, the latest number is about 50% are the BA.4 or BA.5 – mostly BA.5 – subvariants.

sections.label: Pharmaceutical company contracts
sections.summary: Contracts with both pharmaceutical companies allow accepting shipment and implementing them when ready, probably by end of the year, if approved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As of now, our contracts with both pharmaceutical companies do allow us to accept shipment and implement them when ready, probably by end of the year, if they are approved, the data shows it is alright and we receive the shipment.

sections.label: Hospitalisations and surgery cut-backs
sections.summary: Hospitalisation cases have reached almost 700, and cut-back of business-as-usual surgeries, mostly electives, is now about 4%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The number of hospitalisation cases has reached almost 700 now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: At that time, we cut back business-as-usual (BAU) surgeries by 15%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We have now started to trigger some cut-back of BAU, mostly electives, and it is at about 4%.
